findings.title: DOM-based XSS via unescaped JSON object keys
findings.explanation: When rendering a JSON object, json2html() builds the 'keyRepr' HTML fragment directly from the raw object key (`var keyRepr = options.withQuotes ? '"' + key + '"' : key;`) and concatenates it into the output (`html += '' + keyRepr + '';` / `html += keyRepr;`). Unlike string values, which are HTML-escaped at lines 33-38 before being inserted, object property names are never escaped. The resulting HTML string is inserted into the DOM via jQuery's `.html()` call in the jsonViewer plugin method (line 128), which parses and executes any markup it contains. Since this plugin's entire purpose is to render JSON originating from external/untrusted sources (API responses, user-supplied JSON, etc., as shown in demo.html), an attacker who controls any key name in the JSON object (e.g. `{"": 1}`) can inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript that executes in the context of the page embedding the viewer.
